title: Rectangles With the Same Shape

concept.title: The ratio as a reduced fraction
body: Two rectangles have the same shape when their width to height ratios are equal: `w1 / h1 = w2 / h2`. Dividing the numbers gives decimals, which are inexact (`1 / 3` cannot be stored exactly) and different pairs can look alike. Use the **reduced fraction** as the key: divide both `w` and `h` by `gcd(w, h)`. Two ratios are equal exactly when their reduced fractions are equal.

body.code:
g = gcd(w, h)
key = (w // g, h // g)
total += count.get(key, 0)           # a pair with every earlier rectangle of this shape
count[key] = count.get(key, 0) + 1

body: Whenever a "ratio" has to be compared exactly, think of the **reduced fraction** as a hashable key. The same idea is used for slopes of lines. In C++ and Java the pair of numbers can be packed into one 64-bit number, because both parts are below 10^9 + 7.

statement: You are given `n` rectangles with the width `w` and the height `h`. Two rectangles are interchangeable if `w1 / h1 = w2 / h2`. Count the pairs of positions `i < j` of interchangeable rectangles.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has `w` and `h`.

examples.note: All four have the ratio 1 : 2: there are 6 pairs.

hints: Do not use decimal division: it is inexact.
Divide width and height by their gcd to get a reduced fraction.
Count equal fractions with a map, adding the earlier count for every rectangle.

explanation: The reduced fraction `(w / g, h / g)` is an exact key for the ratio; each rectangle pairs with all earlier rectangles with the same key.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log C) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
rect = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

from math import gcd
count = {}
total = 0
for w, h in rect:
    g = gcd(w, h)
    key = (w // g, h // g)
    total += count.get(key, 0)
    count[key] = count.get(key, 0) + 1
print(total)
